title: Shear wave elastography for the non-invasive diagnosis of compartment syndrome: A prospective study on the development of alternative diagnostic procedures
summary: This study investigates how the stiffness of muscles can be measured using shear wave elastography. In a first step, the method is tested on meat samples with different firmness in order to obtain comparative values. This is followed by an examination of healthy volunteers. The muscle stiffness of the thigh and lower leg is first measured at rest and then after physical exertion. The aim is to determine typical values and changes in a physiological range. In future, this reference data could help to recognise compartment syndrome at an early stage, with less pain and less risk.

interventions.name:
Healthy test subjects aged 18-35 years in Germany.
The examinations take place on a single date per participant.
The following examinations are carried out:
- General medical history and information session 
- Biometric data (age, height, weight, BMI)
- Stiffness of the lower leg muscles non-in

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy test subjects >= 18 years and women of childbearing potential with
contraception
Exclusion criteria:
Known pre-existing conditions (cardiac, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, metabolic, kidney and
nervous system), regular cigarette or drug use, pregnant women or regular
medication use (exception: contraception)
